transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, what really pushed me to make this appointment is that I'm having a lot of trouble finishing things at work. 

I'm an auditor, and I just keep starting these follow-up items after my audits or, um, mentorship events. I start them with every intention of finishing them right then. But then I'll find out days later that the final email, or a review note, or some form I needed to submit just... never actually got done. I just keep leaving the final steps unfinished without realizing it, and it's starting to become a real problem.
Has this difficulty finishing tasks been a pattern for you since childhood or adolescence, or is this something that started more recently, say in the past several months?

It's definitely been a pattern since I was young. It's not a new thing at all. 

Even back in elementary school, my report cards would always say that I was bright, but that I lost assignments, or... I rushed past small details. They also mentioned I talked out of turn and always needed reminders to actually finish my work. My mother actually still jokes about it. She says I could completely ace a test, but forget to turn in the project that was sitting right there in my backpack. 

So, yeah, it's been going on for a long time.
Besides the trouble finishing tasks, do you notice yourself feeling restless, needing to move around, or acting impulsively—like interrupting others or making snap decisions—on a regular basis?

Yeah, I definitely get restless. Sitting still for a long time, especially during a long audit review, it just... it feels physically uncomfortable. It's almost like there's this pressure building up inside me. I'll get to a point where I just have to stand up. I'll walk over to the printer, or I'll go get a coffee, or I'll just invent some reason to move around because I can't just sit there anymore.
Do you notice these same difficulties—trouble finishing tasks, restlessness, or impulsivity—affecting other areas of your life outside of work, like at home or in your personal relationships?

Yes, it definitely affects things at home, too. My husband has actually had to take over paying the bills and handling different commitments that I originally agreed to do. He just... he can't count on me to complete them reliably. 

And honestly, the situation at work is really what's stressing me out the most right now. Those mistakes and unfinished follow-ups I mentioned earlier have reached the point where a client review was actually affected. I'm really starting to worry that people are questioning whether I can handle a promotion.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient demonstrates a chronic, childhood-onset pattern of both inattentive symptoms (failing to complete tasks, losing track of follow-up items, careless errors, documented in childhood report cards) and hyperactive-impulsive symptoms (subjective restlessness, inability to remain seated, need to move during long tasks). Both symptom clusters are present concurrently and meet threshold for clinically significant presentation, satisfying criteria for combined presentation ADHD (F90.2) rather than predominantly inattentive (F90.0) or predominantly hyperactive-impulsive (F90.1) subtypes. Impairment is evident across multiple settings (work and home), with functional consequences including workplace performance issues and spousal compensation for household responsibilities.
